rationale: A wins because it gives a founder five usable roads into different desks and is much more disciplined about what proof would make each one real. Its pricing angle, "Figma's new $25 AI seat is a bet that Fortune 500 design teams will pay twice," is a clean SaaS-business story with the right proof asks: adoption, comps, and customer or analyst reaction. B has real bones, but lines like "a company that was weeks away from being absorbed into Adobe" and "That's a different company than Adobe would have built" are invented confidence wearing a strategy blazer.
gaps_in_A: "The Adobe deal died. Figma's answer was to launch its biggest bet yet." overclaims the supplied facts; the update says the launch follows the Adobe collapse, not that Make is Figma's biggest bet or an intentional answer.
"a market that's so far been dominated by smaller AI-native code-generation startups" is an unsourced market-structure claim. If you want that fight, bring named competitors or soften it.
"Figma just picked a fight with every AI tool that turns a prompt into an app" is too broad. Every tool? No. That is headline heat outrunning the evidence.
"automating a specific, common junior task" makes the labor angle sharper than the facts allow. It needs code-quality evidence and hiring-manager proof before it leaves the room.
gaps_in_B: "first major product announcement as a fully independent company" and "weeks away from being absorbed into Adobe" are not in the update. That makes the post-Adobe hook sound reported when it is partly embroidery.
"That's a different company than Adobe would have built" is a counterfactual dressed as insight. No leadership quote, roadmap evidence, or Adobe comparison supports it.
"Vercel's v0, Framer, Webflow, Builder.io" imports a named competitive map the update did not provide. Maybe true, but blind judging punishes maybe.
"no IPO timing disclosed is a meaningful negative signal" overreads an absence. The fact supports not pitching an IPO-timing story, not building investor tea leaves out of silence.
